items.q: Which course pattern best defines acute bacterial rhinosinusitis?
o: Symptoms over 10 days without improvement, severe 3 to 4 day onset, or double worsening
items.exp: Guideline bacterial patterns are persistence, severity or biphasic worsening; coloured mucus alone early is viral. Antibiotics follow these patterns, not discharge colour.
r: Incorrect. Short improving illness is viral.
Correct. Ten days, severe start, or double worsening.
Incorrect. Colour does not equal bacterial day one.
Incorrect. Headache alone fits many causes.
items.kp: Ten, severe, or worse again: bacterial.

items.q: Child with ethmoid sinusitis, proptosis, painful restricted eye movements and chemosis needs what first?
o: Emergency contrast CT, IV antibiotics, ENT and ophthalmology care
items.exp: Post septal orbital cellulitis threatens vision and cavernous spread; imaging grades Chandler stage guiding drainage. Preseptal disease keeps normal movements, vision and no proptosis.
r: Incorrect. Orbital signs exceed oral home care.
Correct. Scan, IV treat, joint specialist care.
Incorrect. Movement pain excludes simple preseptal.
Incorrect. Drops cannot treat orbit.
items.kp: Painful proptosed eye with sinusitis scans now.

items.q: Forehead swelling in adolescent with frontal sinusitis (Pott puffy tumour) represents what?
o: Frontal bone osteomyelitis with subperiosteal abscess
items.exp: Pott puffy tumour is frontal osteomyelitis via diploic veins with subperiosteal collection, risking epidural abscess; it needs imaging, IV antibiotics and surgical drainage planning.
r: Incorrect. Allergy lacks fever bony swelling context.
Correct. Frontal osteomyelitis collection.
Incorrect. Bite lacks sinusitis linkage.
Incorrect. Polyps live intranasally.
items.kp: Puffy forehead over bad sinus is bone pus.

items.q: Bilateral chemosis, ophthalmoplegia and sepsis after sinusitis indicate which complication?
items.exp: Cavernous sinuses communicate across midline, so bilateral eye signs with trigeminal involvement and septic course after sphenoid or ethmoid disease define this lethal thrombosis needing MRI/MRV and ICU care.
r: Incorrect. Preseptal is unilateral lid only.
Correct. Cavernous sinus thrombosis bilateralises.
Incorrect. Conjunctivitis spares movements and proptosis.
Incorrect. Tear sac infection localises medial canthus.
items.kp: Both eyes involved: cavernous sinus clotting.

items.q: Persistent one sided foul maxillary sinusitis in adult should prompt examination of what?
o: Upper premolar and molar roots (odontogenic source)
items.exp: Upper posterior tooth roots abut or protrude into maxillary floor; periapical infection or oroantral fistula after extraction sustains unilateral sinusitis until dental treatment plus sinus care.
r: Incorrect. Lower teeth drain elsewhere.
Correct. Upper back teeth infect maxillary sinus.
Incorrect. Tonsils cause pharyngeal symptoms.
Incorrect. Parotid is cheek gland.
items.kp: One bad maxilla: look at upper teeth.

items.q: Frontal sinus is typically absent or rudimentary until about what age, shaping paediatric sinusitis patterns?
o: Pneumatises through childhood, clinically relevant from about 6 to 7 years
items.exp: Ethmoid and maxillary sinuses exist at birth (ethmoid causing childhood orbital complications), sphenoid develops mid childhood and frontal last into teens, so frontal disease and Pott tumour are older child or adolescent problems.
r: Incorrect. Frontal sinus is not formed at birth.
Correct. Frontal develops from school age.
Incorrect. Thirty is far too late.
Incorrect. Most adults have frontal sinuses (some aplasia).
items.kp: Ethmoids trouble toddlers; frontals trouble teens.

items.q: FESS (functional endoscopic sinus surgery) aims principally to do what?
o: Restore ventilation and mucociliary drainage at ostiomeatal complex
Replace antibiotics in acute viral colds
items.exp: FESS widens natural ostia and clears diseased ethmoid partitions preserving mucosa and cilia function for chronic or complicated disease failing medical therapy. It is not acute cold treatment.
r: Incorrect. Mucosa preservation is principle.
Correct. Restore natural drainage pathways.
Incorrect. Obliteration is rare salvage.
Incorrect. Viral colds need no surgery.
items.kp: Open the natural doors, keep the lining.

items.q: Most common sinus involved in acute bacterial sinusitis of adults is what?
items.exp: Maxillary sinusitis dominates adult practice (large sinus, dependent ostium high on medial wall impairing drainage). Isolated sphenoid disease is uncommon but dangerous by neighbours.
r: Incorrect. Frontal follows maxillary frequency.
Correct. Maxillary commonest.
Incorrect. Isolated sphenoid is rare.
Incorrect. Sinuses are the disease site.

items.q: Danger neighbours making isolated sphenoid sinusitis high risk are what?
o: Cavernous sinus, internal carotid, pituitary and optic nerve
items.exp: Sphenoid walls border cavernous carotid, pituitary fossa and optic nerve, so infection or surgical slips threaten vision, major bleeding and hypopituitarism; deep vertex headache is clue.
r: Incorrect. Teeth neighbour maxillary floor.
Correct. Carotid, pituitary, optic, cavernous sinus.
Incorrect. Parotid is lateral face.
Incorrect. Tonsil is oropharyngeal.
items.kp: Sphenoid sits among giants: respect it.

items.q: Routine CT scanning in uncomplicated acute viral rhinosinusitis is what?
o: Not indicated; imaging reserved for complications, recurrence, immunocompromise or surgical planning
items.exp: Imaging in simple colds shows incidental mucosal thickening without changing care and adds radiation; endoscopy and course patterns guide, scanning follows red flags.
r: Incorrect. Not for simple viral illness.
Correct. Reserve CT for defined indications.
Incorrect. Examination remains primary.
Incorrect. Discharge colour never mandates scan.
items.kp: No red flags, no sinus scan.
